packages.section: the lead's fix list in this note (from F-punk's 1 m sheets beside Street Punk A), within Part C §7 'F-punk' and the slice gate's locks
packages.note: You own tools/pipeline/** EXCEPT tools/pipeline/player_*.py and the body_objects() function of tools/pipeline/blender_export.py (F-player-fix adds a third player mesh there), assets/*/characters/punk/**, assets/source/palette/punk.json, the ASSETS.md Punk rows, tests/test_art_punk.gd, the Punk rows of tests/test_art_contract.gd (not its mesh-name allow-list, which is F-player-fix's), game/actors/art/punk_art.tres and its variants, and docs/milestones/M4-calls/F-punk.md. Fixes, from the lead's look at captures/final/c2 and c4 (1600x900, the guard at 1 m): (1) The gloves. The concept has dark fingerless gloves with DARK wrist cuffs and no yellow; ours have a wide yellow-banded gauntlet ring with black slivers at its edge, which reads as a spiked bracelet and is the noisiest thing in the frame. Recolour the strap and cuff band to the glove's dark family (a second charcoal slot only if the border needs it to ink), remove the slivers, and trim the cuff's bulk as far as the A9 4 pp lens-share bar allows; keep the glove swatch value at about 0.3 or more so its bands read. (2) The shades. punk_lens and punk_yellow are the same #e8bd2e, so the head reads as one yellow mass from the crown to the cheek. The concept has gold lenses in a dark frame. Separate them: a dark frame line (the detail mask or its own slot) and, if needed, a lens value or hue distinct from the cap (no red, A13); the lens stays marks-off. (3) Face speckle: tune detail_bake (ink_low, ink_high and the face's settings) so the nose line and mouth mark stay and the skin speckle goes. (4) Blotches: the toon bands break into dark patches on the vest and on the forearms in the guard (lumpy generated normals or stray palette cells). Clear them by smoothing normals (not positions) or a palette-cell cleanup on the torso and arms, without softening the silhouette or moving A6. Keep the boots and laces per the concept if they drifted (cream high-tops, yellow laces). Leave the waist-hem stretch ratchet, the slim-thigh clamp and gap 3's knuckle facing as they are unless a fix above moves them. Re-export over punk.glb (and rebuild the three variants so they stay comparable), re-run run.py --check, run the full suite (it must stay green), and re-record C1, C2, C4, C5, C6 and C11 (one act per process). Done: the four fixes visible in full-resolution 1 m stills beside the concept, with an honest before/after per fix.

packages.section: the lead's fix list in this note (from F-player-art's first-person sheets beside Hero C), within Part A §A14 and F-player-int's contract
packages.note: You own assets/source/characters/player/**, assets/export/characters/player/**, assets/source/palette/player.json, tools/pipeline/player_*.py, the body_objects() function of tools/pipeline/blender_export.py (only to return Body__fp_torso too), the mesh-name allow-list in tests/test_art_contract.gd, tests/test_art_player.gd, game/camera/first_person_camera.gd (only _find_torso_meshes() and what Body__fp_torso needs), the ASSETS.md player rows, and docs/milestones/M4-calls/F-player-art.md. Fixes: (1) The straight punches. In pa1's jab, cross and hook strike frames the elbow half of the bare upper arm fills about a third of the view and ends in the split's flat inward cap with a fan of ink lines, so it reads as a stump. The probe mannequin frames the same way (it is M3's camera and arm geometry, and M3 keeps the elbow end on purpose: placeholder_body.gd, FP_HIDDEN_PARTS), so keep the cut where it is but make it read like M3's Elbow capsule: a rounded dome cap at the cut with smooth normals, no crease or border ink on the cap, and the skin's swatch. Smooth the visible upper arm's normals so its bands don't blotch. Print the own arm's view share in those strike frames before and after, beside the probe's. (2) The fists. The fingers are 3-4-triangle lumps at 0.3-0.6 m and the glove/skin border is ragged. Clean the fist's label boundaries (a majority filter or smoothing of the region border), and you may raise each fist to 4,000 triangles (the total stays under 30,000) and spend at most one T13 retry (50 credits) if the generated piece itself is the limit. (3) The front kick. The shin and shoe merge into one near-black shape with a sawtooth band edge: lift the shoe's black to a charcoal of value about 0.25-0.3 (the concept's shoes are black slip-ons with cream soles) so its bands and ink read, and keep the slate trousers distinct. (4) Body__fp_torso: the third mesh (Spine and Hips: the belly and belt) as F-player-int asked, so fp_knockdown_hide_torso hides only the belly. That needs body_objects() in blender_export.py, the contract's allow-list, a second plane cut with caps in player_parts.py split, and FirstPersonCamera._find_torso_meshes(). Measure the knockdown's view share with the toggle off and on, on the hero, and print both. (5) The red test. tests/test_art_player.gd's 'the plan's A9 against the proxies' fails on the hero (12 of 15 poses against FPView's looser proxies). The lead's call: give the hero the probe's treatment, a ratchet at the hero's own figures after your fixes (cells, share and the nearer-than-the-proxies'-own-meshes distance), each printing the plan's exact bars as GATE lines, as the gate's lock 3 does for the Punk. The suite must be green. Re-export player.glb and player_detail.png, re-run player_run.py --check, run the full suite, and re-record pa1, pa2 and T8 ('Look: tune own hull') on it. Done: full-resolution first-person stills of the jab, cross, hook, look-down 65, guard and front kick beside the last round's, with an honest read of each.
